messages.subject: Log idiom
parts:

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: Log idiom
parts:
Hmm you can disregard this one. Nothing I was doing to get
information out of a map-reduce job was working and I finally figured
out why.

In the context of using my experimental map/reduce as environments
system (since the original posting it has been modified but the jist
of which is posted here), I was getting an error at the time of the
map environment attach before the map functions got called. Hence,
every strategy I used to get information out of the system inside the
map functions failed because the code never got called.

BTW if your wondering how an attach can make an error, it was because
I was trying to pass a subset argument and the subset needs to be
evaluated in the environment of data.frames in the map.keys. I got a
plan for that though.

Since I realized that, I can now get the info I need.

Thanks,
Jeremiah

messages.subject: Re: Log idiom
parts:
I gave up on the logging when I figured out how to get my dump error
scheme to work again (I struggled with permissions on the cluster
until I thought it through clearly). First thing I do now in setup
prior to any possible error is use:

errorFunc = function() {
local = ""
try({if(!is.null(map.values)) local = "map."},silent=TRUE)
try({if(!is.null(reduce.values)) local = "reduce."},silent=TRUE)
uniqueid = paste(sample(letters,10,replace=TRUE),sep="",collapse="")
filename = paste("error.env.",local, uniqueid,".RData",sep="")
save.image(filename)
errdir = "/wsc/tmp/jrounds/error/"
#need to make the directory ahead of time and set permissions for
hadoop user to write.
system(paste("hadoop dfs -put", filename, errdir))
fullname = paste(errdir,filename,sep="")
system(paste("hadoop dfs -chown jrounds", fullname))
}
options(error = errorFunc)

After an error occurs errdir has one Rdata file per a simultaneously
running job (tested on a cluster).

That seems to work quite well on the cluster. Makes a directory of
error environments for inspection if there is an error. I previously
mentioned it. I just hadn't got around to getting the idea to work on
the cluster yet. The only reason I mentioned on this thread is that
it is a personal narrative and explains why I abandoned any concept of
a log. Though I guess the corollary to the question "how do you log
in a distributed environment?" has the answer: one log per a process
in a log directory. That is really what I have with the saved
environments. One environment per a process given it created an
error. Up to the user to inspect them for bugs.
